summary: Douglas County, OR summit in the Umpqua NF: 20-ft L-4 tower 1932, removed 1958; the 1942 AWS cabin survives and is a Forest Service cabin, closed for structural issues.

facts.design: 20-foot round fir pole tower with L-4 cab (1932)
facts.status_note: Tower and cab removed in 1958; the 1942 AWS cabin and outbuildings were kept and still stand

access.note: The Forest Service cabin page says it is closed due to structural issues and will stay closed for maintenance until further notice. No access is described for the tower site

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. The Forest Service recommends a high-clearance or four-wheel-drive vehicle, and roads are not plowed in winter

November 7, 1929 Glendale Log: a lookout fireman on Butler Butte was held in service some weeks after the fire season closed, to survey the extent of the summit ridge fire
20-foot round fir pole tower with L-4 cab, replacing the 1920 crow's nest and cab

Register: tower removed in 1958. Forest Lookouts: tower and cab removed, AWS cabin and outbuildings retained. Firelookout.com: tower destroyed in 1958
Registered November 24, 2010 as US 774, OR 183; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts gives activation August 24, 1942; the Forest Service page says the tower was used by AWS from early 1942. The story gives both.

Firelookout.com says the AWS cabin is still there and available on the Recreation Rental program. The Forest Service page says the cabin is closed due to structural issues. The story reports the Forest Service page as the current notice; the cabin stands in both. The Forest Service page carries no date in the cache copy.
Register and Forest Lookouts say the tower was removed in 1958; Firelookout.com says it was destroyed in 1958. Same year, different wording.

notes_for_editor: Brief status gone is right for the tower; the brief's firelookout_com=standing conflict is the surviving 1942 AWS cabin, not a standing tower. Brief access was unknown; the cabin's closure notice is the access fact used. Recreation.gov listing for the cabin (campsites/80024) was seen in search only, not read; its current availability was not checked. The Forest Service page is undated in the cache. Verification 2026-10-09: the 1932 tower is cited to the register and Forest Lookouts only, since Firelookout.com has no quote for it; the 1929 Glendale Log item is about a lookout fireman, not the lookout itself; the cabin rental is $40 per night per group.
